# Actual three-layer root concavity fails inside the endpoint Minkowski section

The endpoint-only theorem `candidate 0fcbc670d417c3ed` does not extend to the full actual three-layer depth even when the candidate points remain strictly inside the endpoint Minkowski section. This fails in d=2 with positively homothetic simplex endpoints of unequal volumes. The middle enlargement is convex-compatible, nonnested with the larger endpoint, and no fiber has half the total mass.

## 1. The exact body

Let T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}, set delta=1/8, and define

    A=T,
    C=2T,
    D=(A+C)/2=(3/2)T,
    B=(-delta,-delta)+(7/4)T.

Equivalently,

    B={x_1>=-1/8, x_2>=-1/8, x_1+x_2<=3/2}.

Consequently D subset B. The body

    C_actual=conv(({−1} times A) union ({0} times B)
                                      union ({1} times C))

is full-dimensional in R^3 and has exactly those three integer fibers. At base zero, a convex combination of the two endpoint fibers contributes only points of D, already in B, so the middle fiber is exactly B. Its mixed set has full positive planar fibers and C_actual equals the convex hull of that set.

The endpoint shapes are positively homothetic simplices; their translations here are zero. B and C are incomparable: (-1/8,-1/8) is in B but outside C, whereas (2,0) is in C but outside B. The exact areas are

    a=|A|=1/2,  U=|B|=49/32,  b=|C|=2,
    M=a+U+b=129/32.

The largest individual volume is 2<129/64=M/2. Thus this is an actual asymmetric, nonheavy three-fiber configuration, rather than a two-layer source or a dominant-fiber simplification.

## 2. Exact all-cap depth along an interior segment

For 0<t<=1/3 put y_t=(t,t). Every such point belongs to int(D). We claim the actual ABSOLUTE mixed depth at (0,y_t) is exactly

    P(t)=4t^2+2(t+delta)^2
        =6t^2+4delta t+2delta^2.                         (1)

For the lower bound, both endpoint bodies contain L_t=3tT, whose ordinary centroid is y_t and whose area is 9t^2/2. For any ambient cap through (0,y_t), its two endpoint traces are opposite scalar thresholds about that centroid. The already proved paired-centroid-tail theorem gives a total of at least

    2 Gamma_2 |L_t|=2(4/9)(9t^2/2)=4t^2                 (2)

from the two endpoint copies. If the continuous normal vanishes, the cap contains at least one whole L_t, which is larger than the bound (2). This explicitly retains every integer tilt and both cap orientations.

The middle body contains

    E_t=(-delta,-delta)+3(t+delta)T.

Its centroid is also y_t. The containment follows from

    3(t+delta)<=3(1/3+1/8)=11/8<7/4.

Ordinary Grünbaum therefore gives at least

    Gamma_2 |E_t|=(4/9)(9(t+delta)^2/2)
                       =2(t+delta)^2                  (3)

from the middle fiber in every containing cap. Adding (2)--(3) proves the lower bound in (1), with one and the same point y_t.

For the matching upper bound use the SINGLE closed ambient cap

    H_t={x_1+x_2<=2t},                                  (4)

with zero integer coefficient. Its A and C traces are both 2tT, each of area 2t^2. Its B trace is (-delta,-delta)+2(t+delta)T, of area 2(t+delta)^2. All are proper triangles in the indicated t range. Hence the mass of (4) equals (1). This proves exact global minimization over every containing halfspace at every y_t; it is not a fixed-slope numerical test.

## 3. A rational three-point certificate

Choose

    t_0=1/16,  t_m=1/8,  t_1=3/16.

These are strictly interior points of D, with y_(t_m)=(y_(t_0)+y_(t_1))/2. Equation (1) gives

    P(t_0)=11/128,
    P(t_m)=24/128=3/16,
    P(t_1)=43/128.

The proposed d-root concavity, with d=2, would require

    sqrt(24)>=(sqrt(11)+sqrt(43))/2.

This is false: after squaring it would imply 21>=sqrt(473), whereas 21^2=441<473. Thus root concavity fails strictly INSIDE D, unlike the earlier interval counter whose last point lies outside the endpoint Minkowski section.

More generally the square root of (1) is strictly convex throughout this segment. For P(t)=6t^2+4delta t+2delta^2,

    2P(t)P''(t)-P'(t)^2=32delta^2>0.

The endpoint-only contribution in (2) has a linear square root, and so does the middle lower bound in (3). Their sum has nonconcave square root because these two linear roots have different zero locations. Actual containment of D in B does not force those locations to agree.

## 4. This is not a depth counterexample

The required OC absolute target for this source is

    Gamma_2 M/2=43/48.

There is an explicit actual middle point with every cap having mass at least 1>43/48. Take y=(1/2,1/2), the centroid of D. The middle contribution is at least Gamma_2 |D|=(4/9)(9/8)=1/2.

Moreover A subset 2y-C: the reflected large triangle is

    2y-C={x_1<=1, x_2<=1, x_1+x_2>=0},

which contains T. For any paired endpoint cap, the two reflected portions on A are complementary, so the pair captures at least |A|=1/2. Equivalently this is the exact reflected-containment median-set criterion in `candidate e18e6db2f3e079d5`. Vertical caps also contain the whole middle fiber plus an endpoint. Adding the two half-unit bounds proves the claim.

Thus the example closes a specific proposed strengthening: even nonheavy unequal homothetic simplex endpoints and a compatible middle enlargement do not make the FULL mixed depth's dth root concave on their Minkowski section. The endpoint-only center-motion theorem and its sum-of-two-powers lower bound remain valid. No inference about the general three-fiber OC problem follows from this failure.

All geometry, areas, exact cap values, containment inequalities and the radical comparison are checked with fractions in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_three_layer_root_concavity_inside_minkowski.py`. The all-cap lower bound uses precisely the already audited paired-centroid-tail theorem and ordinary triangle Grünbaum.
